WITH item_town AS (
  SELECT ili.order_item_id, c.town_city,
         AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_price,
         AVG(ili.derived_product_cost * 1.0 / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Invoices i ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number
  JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town AS (
  SELECT town_city, AVG(avg_price) AS avg_price, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM item_town
  GROUP BY town_city
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_ratio FROM town
)
SELECT t.town_city, t.avg_price, t.avg_ratio, t.avg_ratio - o.overall_ratio AS ratio_excess
FROM town t CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE t.avg_ratio > o.overall_ratio;

assumptions.assumption: The cross-town average ratio is the simple average of the per-town average ratios, so each town counts equally. Towns whose ratio is entirely missing are excluded from that average.
A zero derived_total_cost gives a missing ratio (NULLIF), so it is ignored like any other missing value.
Customers with a NULL town_city form their own group and are included in the town averages.

alternatives.interpretation: The cross-town average is taken over all (order item, town) averages, so each item-town pair counts equally rather than each town.

assumptions.assumption: The 'average of that ratio across all towns' is the unweighted mean of the per-town average ratios (each town counts once), not a mean over all items or lines.
The ratio derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost is computed per line as a decimal. A zero total cost gives NULL, which is ignored, as are NULL prices and costs.
Lines are linked to the customer through Invoices.order_id, then Orders.customer_id. Towns with a NULL town_city form their own group.
